drivers.description: Attack From Mars (1.1 Pinball FX / S1.1)

mechanisms.behavior: Four balls rest on opto switches 32-35 with switch 31 at the jam/eject position. Trough eject (solenoid 2, assembly A-19963-1) delivers to the shooter lane (switch 18); the auto plunger (solenoid 1, A-14525) launches. During an active ball saver the replacement serve fires within roughly 100 ms of the drain; with a trivial bonus count the next player's serve can follow a drain in as little as 1.6 s, so serve classification must not rely on timing alone.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: Every saucer entry - wave hits and final destruction alike - closes switch 78 'Center Trough' under the UFO; the ball exits via subway to the left popper (switch 36) and is ejected up a vertical tube by solenoid 3 (A-20633). The saucer shake motor (solenoid 15, A-20608) wobbles the UFO in pulse bursts; on saucer destruction a burst of roughly 5-7 pulses about 0.25 s apart runs, and the ROM raises the 3-bank motor wall at roughly pulse 5, before the burst ends. For locks 1 and 2 the ROM keeps the locked ball in the left popper and serves a replacement from the trough; lock 3 releases for multiball.
mechanisms.label: UFO saucer with subway return

mechanisms.behavior: Standup targets 45-47 ride a motorized wall (output 24, motor part 14-8023 driven from a flasher-class circuit) traveling between limit switches 66 (down) and 67 (up). The ROM raises the bank mid destruction animation while the saucer-shake burst is still running; recreations ejecting the left popper in that window must mind the moving bank geometry.
mechanisms.label: Three-target motor bank

mechanisms.behavior: Four pop-up alien figures (assemblies A-20579-1/-2) cover the seven MARTIAN standup targets: solenoid 5 'Left Alien Low' covers M-A-R (switches 56-58), solenoid 6 'Left Alien High' covers MARTI"A"N (switch 43 zone), solenoid 8 'Right Alien High' covers MARTIA"N" (switch 44 zone), and solenoid 14 'Right Alien Low' covers T-I (switches 41-42).
mechanisms.label: Pop-up aliens over MARTIAN standups

mechanisms.behavior: Single center drop target (switch 77) with reset coil solenoid 16 (assembly A-20657).
mechanisms.label: Single center drop target

mechanisms.behavior: Stroke-of-Luck scoop: capture on switch 37, award, then eject by solenoid 4 (assembly A-20573 with LED/photo-transistor ball detection).
mechanisms.label: Right popper (Stroke of Luck scoop)

mechanisms.behavior: One-way loop control gates (coil A-14406, gate assembly A-17796): solenoid 33 'Right Gate' on a high-power circuit, solenoid 34 'Left Gate' on a low-power circuit; loop travel is sensed by the high/low loop switch pairs 71/72 and 73/74.
mechanisms.label: Loop gates

mechanisms.behavior: Ramp diverter (assembly A-20099) on a power-plus-hold coil pair: solenoid 35 'Diverter Power' (high power) pulls in, solenoid 36 'Diverter Hold' (low power) holds. Opens to divert center-ramp shots to the lock when a lock is lit (lamp 54 'Light Lock' solid).
mechanisms.label: Center ramp diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Backpanel strobe tube (output 39, Strobe Lamp/Strobe Tube P.C.B.s) plus a 16-LED chase chain (16-LED Chase & Flasher P.C.B.) controlled serially via outputs 37 'L.E.D. Clock' and 38 'L.E.D. Data'. Used prominently by Strobe Multiball.
mechanisms.label: Strobe light and LED chase chain

physical.notes: Address assignment follows the retained known-working g5k script, which binds SolCallback(33) to the right gate and SolCallback(34) to the left gate. Pinned PinMAME names them the other way round: src/wpc/sims/wpc/full/afm.c maps sLGate to WPC_FLIPPERCOIL95 bit 0x10 (public solenoid 33) and sRGate to bit 0x20 (public solenoid 34). PinMAME's own naming is also internally inconsistent with its custom-solenoid aliases, so the left/right labels here rest on the manual and the proven script, and the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged. The retained manual settles the naming: solenoid/flasher table page 2-46 (PDF 140) lists '33 RIGHT GATE, High Power, Q84, J120-6, Yel-Vio, A-14406' and '34 LEFT GATE, Low Power, Q86, J120-4, Org-Vio, A-14406', and the same page's flipper-circuit block assigns the identical transistor/connector/wire (Q84/J120-6/Yel-Vio power, Q86/J120-4/Org-Vio hold) to the unused upper-right flipper circuit these gates ride. Manual and known-working script agree; the pinned-PinMAME sLGate/sRGate names are swapped relative to both. The Solenoid/Flasher Locations continuation on page 2-47 (PDF 141) independently lists item 33 (coil A-14406, assembly A-17796) as 'Right Gate' and item 34 as 'Left Gate'.

WPC-95 LPDC output; PinMAME mirrors it at public address 43, so 39 and 43 are one physical output.

PinMAME duplicates the WPC-95 LPDC outputs 37-40 at public addresses 41-44 (src/wpc/core.c core_getSol, GEN_WPC95|GEN_WPC95DCS), so public solenoid 43 reports the same physical output as public solenoid 39. It is not a second saucer-dome circuit. The retained g5k script binds SolModCallback(39) and SolModCallback(43) to two different visual lamps, which is a table convenience rather than two physical circuits, and any runtime observation of 43 is fully explained by the mirror.

outputs.label: Custom Solenoid Alias of Public Solenoid 34

physical.notes: afmGameData declares custSol=3, so PinMAME publishes game-specific solenoids 51-53 for Attack From Mars in addition to the standard range. afm_getSol returns WPC_FLIPPERCOIL95 bit 0x20 for this address, which is the same bit core_getSol reports on public solenoid 34. This address is therefore a duplicate view of an already-declared circuit, not an extra physical device.

This address is therefore a duplicate view of an already-declared circuit, not an extra physical device.

physical.notes: afmGameData declares custSol=3, so PinMAME publishes game-specific solenoids 51-53 for Attack From Mars in addition to the standard range. afm_getSol returns WPC_FLIPPERCOIL95 bits 0xc0 for this address, which is the combined state of public solenoids 35 and 36. This address is therefore a duplicate view of an already-declared circuit, not an extra physical device.
